items.headline: Putin's First Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Sparks Diplomatic Protest from Japan
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin made his first personal visit to the disputed Kuril Islands on Thursday, touring facilities on Iturup Island following regional naval exercises [2.1.3]. The trip prompted an immediate diplomatic protest from Japan, which claims sovereignty over the territory and considers the visit unacceptable.

items.headline: Taiwan Reports Near-Autonomous AI Cyberattack Targeting Government and Infrastructure
items.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs and cybersecurity researchers disclosed a multi-day cyberattack in which open-source AI agents breached government systems, a nuclear safety agency, and energy providers. The incident marks one of the first publicly documented cases of a near-autonomous AI campaign targeting state infrastructure, raising urgent global concerns about AI-driven threats.

items.headline: Six Arab Football Federations Back Embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino
items.summary: Six Arab soccer federations have officially declared their support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino as he faces pressure to resign from several regional governing bodies. The governance crisis follows widespread backlash over a controversial proposal to sell a commercial stake in World Cup rights to private investors.

items.headline: Academy Museum Names Charlize Theron, Colman Domingo, and John Carpenter 2026 Gala Honorees
items.summary: The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures announced on August 13 that Charlize Theron, Colman Domingo, and John Carpenter will be honored at its sixth annual fundraising gala on October 17, 2026. Theron will receive the Icon Award, Carpenter the Luminary Award, and Domingo the Vantage Award in recognition of their major contributions to global cinema.
